# Documents current behavior in a nested layout: git fires the pre-commit hook
# for EVERY commit in the repository, not only for commits touching the sesam
# dir. An unsealed plaintext edit under vault/ is therefore sealed and staged
# into whatever commit comes next - here one that only touches app/.
#
# In a standalone secrets repo this is the intended auto-seal. In a monorepo it
# means unrelated commits silently carry vault changes. If that is not wanted,
# the hook should only seal+stage when the index already touches the sesam dir
# and otherwise just warn about the pending seal; flip the assertions below.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir app
cp appfile app/index.js
mkdir vault
exec sesam init --user admin --sesam-dir vault
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init monorepo with nested sesam'

# Half-edited secret (not sealed), plus a staged change elsewhere in the monorepo.
cp changed vault/README.md
cp appfile2 app/index.js
exec git add app/index.js

# git would run this from the worktree root with the baked-in --sesam-dir.
exec sesam --sesam-dir vault hook pre-commit

# The hook sealed the drifted secret and staged it next to the app change.
exec git diff --cached --name-only
stdout 'app/index\.js'
stdout 'vault/\.sesam/objects/README\.md\.sesam'
stdout 'vault/\.sesam/audit/log\.jsonl'

-- appfile --
console.log(1)
-- appfile2 --
console.log(2)
-- changed --
# changed readme
